title: Frevo umbrella dance
summary: A fast carnival dance from Brazil in which dancers leap, crouch and kick while twirling a small colourful umbrella to a brass march.
howToPlay: Four places are lit beside the dancer: Twirl for the umbrella, Kick, Crouch and Leap.
A ring closes on a place when that movement is due. Tap the place as the ring closes and the dancer answers with the move.
Start with the street steps, then try the low and high figure and the parade round.
rules: A tap right on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and taps with no ring open cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through; every pattern is counted in fours at march tempo.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the dance, not choreography to copy.
heritageNote: Frevo grew in the carnival streets of Recife and Olinda, where dancers answered the brass bands with athletic steps. The little umbrella, once a way to keep balance in a crowd, became the dance's signature and is thrown, twirled and passed between hands.
